learn.canDo: Size an eval set for the smallest change that matters, cover rare input kinds on purpose, and keep it out of the prompt.
learn.why: Every AI team is asked how it knows a change helped. A trustworthy eval set is the answer.
learn.keyIdea: Enough examples, the right ones, kept apart.

learn.canDo: Choose and validate code-based graders, weighing false fails against false passes.
learn.why: Code graders are fast and repeatable, but a bad one quietly lies. Measuring its errors is the expert move.
learn.keyIdea: Grade the meaning, not the typography.

learn.canDo: Set up an LLM judge with a rubric, counter its biases, and calibrate it against human labels.
learn.why: Judges scale evaluation and mislead when unchecked. Knowing the biases and how to measure agreement is the core skill.

learn.canDo: Build a regression gate whose noise is below the effect, using paired comparisons and a threshold between effect and noise.
learn.why: Flaky prompt tests teach teams to ignore them. Understanding the statistics keeps the gate honest.
learn.keyIdea: A gate sees only changes bigger than its noise.

learn.canDo: Layer offline suites, shadow traffic and guarded live tests, and compute the users exposed at each stage.
learn.why: Offline passes can hide regressions in slices the suite lacks. Layered testing is how production teams ship safely.
learn.keyIdea: Shadow tests what you say; live tests what users do.

learn.canDo: Design a complete release gate: suite, graders, calibrated judge, pairing, threshold and guarded canary, within a budget.
learn.why: Shipping a prompt safely uses every eval skill at once. The skill is finding the weakest link in the gate.
learn.keyIdea: Find the weakest link in the gate.

chapter.story: Pigeon's prompts start changing weekly, and the team needs to know whether each change helped.
outcomes: Build eval sets that can be trusted
Choose graders and judges and measure their errors
Gate prompt changes without crying wolf
Test on real traffic without hurting real users
chapter.why: Without evals, prompt work is opinion. Each tool here removes a way to fool yourself.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can describe how you would know a prompt change is safe to ship. At work you will argue from a measured gate instead of three examples.
